message.content:
Build 'Status notices': a library of PREMADE customer-facing notices the owner can switch ON and OFF with one click, for moments like 'we are experiencing a large number of deployments right now, so deployments may be slightly delayed' or 'we are under a lot of load'. Notes to /root/agent-notes/status-notices.md; final report at the end.

HARD RULES: read /root/agent-briefs/growth-batch-2026-10-02.md first, all its rules apply (no prod DB writes from scripts, no node/VM changes, no secrets in logs, explicit-path commits, never `git add -A`, build in a git worktree on /tank off main e.g. `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/nxeon-wt-notices -b feature/status-notices main`, cp -a node_modules, dummy DATABASE_URL for prisma generate, heavy lock, no builds in /opt/nxeon). Schema changes ADDITIVE only. Do not merge to main; do not deploy; the owner session integrates. Never disable the sandbox: if something cannot reach a node, tell the owner session. Nxeon speaks as the owner: customer-facing text never says 'provider' or implies a third party runs our infrastructure; no fabricated stats or ETAs.

WHAT EXISTS (read first, extend, do NOT build a second system): model Announcement + AnnouncementDismissal in prisma/schema.prisma (title, body, level INFO|SUCCESS|WARNING|CRITICAL, active, startsAt, expiresAt, createdBy), lib/actions-announcements.ts (create/publish/unpublish/delete, getUnseenAnnouncements, what's-new), lib/actions-broadcast.ts (activeAnnouncementsForUser, the admin broadcast actions), app/admin/broadcast/page.tsx and app/admin/announcements/page.tsx (admin UI), components/customer/AnnouncementBanner.tsx rendered in app/dashboard/layout.tsx (dismissible per user), the deploy wizard (components/nx/DeployView.tsx, app/dashboard/deploy/*), the public Status link in the nav (find the /status page if one exists), lib/rbac.ts + lib/admin-nav.ts for which admin area gates broadcast, lib/settings.ts for settings conventions.

BUILD:
1. A premade catalog in code (lib/status-notices.ts, plain data, no I/O) of about 16 to 20 presets, each with: stable `key`, `label` (admin-facing), `category`, `level`, customer-facing `title` and `body` (plain, calm, honest, short), `placement` ('dashboard' banner, 'deploy' = shown inside the order/deploy flow, or both), `defaultDurationHours` (null = until switched off), `dismissible`. Categories and presets to include (write the text well, in Nxeon's voice, no invented numbers):
   Deployments: 'High deployment volume' (a lot of servers are being deployed right now, so setup may take a few extra minutes; your order is safe and will complete), 'Provisioning slower than usual', 'Game server deployments delayed', 'Region at capacity' (new orders in the region are limited; suggest another region) and a per-region variant generated from the real regions/nodes (Singapore, Canada, Germany) so the owner can switch each on separately, 'Deployments paused briefly'.
   Platform: 'We are investigating an issue', 'Degraded performance', 'Control panel slow', 'Console or Files tab slow', 'Email delivery delayed', 'Login or signup issues'.
   Billing: 'Payments delayed' (card or wallet top-ups may take longer to show), 'Local payment methods unavailable'.
   Maintenance: 'Scheduled maintenance' (generic, with an editable window), 'Emergency maintenance', 'Node maintenance'.
   Support: 'Support replies slower than usual'.
   Positive: 'All clear: issue resolved' (SUCCESS, auto-expires in 6 hours).
   Plus 'Custom notice' (free text).
2. Admin UI: a 'Quick notices' section at the TOP of /admin/broadcast (and linked from admin nav/settings) showing the presets grouped by category as cards with a clear ON/OFF switch, current state, who switched it and when, an optional 'turn off automatically after N hours' selector (default from the preset), and 'Edit text' to override title/body BEFORE switching on (kept per notice). Switching ON creates or reactivates the Announcement row for that preset (additive column `templateKey String? @unique` on Announcement, plus `placement String @default("dashboard")` and `dismissible Boolean @default(true)`), OFF deactivates it (keep history). Idempotent, race-safe (unique key + upsert), writes an audit log entry for every toggle with the actor, and respects the same admin permission that broadcast uses. Show a live 'Right now' hint next to the Deployments presets: the number of PROVISION jobs that are QUEUED or RUNNING and the age of the oldest queued one (read from the Job table), so the owner can decide; do NOT auto-enable anything (an optional setting 'status_notice_auto_suggest' may only highlight the suggested preset in the admin UI when the queue depth or oldest-queued age crosses thresholds; default OFF behaviour is just the hint).
3. Customer display: (a) the existing dashboard banner keeps working for placement 'dashboard' and 'both' (respect dismissal only when dismissible; WARNING/CRITICAL deployment notices should NOT be dismissible); (b) for placement 'deploy' and 'both', render a clear inline notice at the TOP of the deploy wizard and again next to the final pay/confirm step so a customer sees it before paying, and on the order success/provisioning screen ('Your server is being set up. Deployments are taking longer than usual right now, this is expected.'); (c) if a public /status page exists, list active notices there too (no dismiss). Notices may carry a region so the Singapore notice appears only when the customer selected Singapore (use the deploy wizard's selected region; for the generic ones show always). Accessible (role=status/alert as appropriate), on-theme, mobile friendly, no layout shift.
4. Safety/honesty: switching a notice on must never block orders (it is information only); expired notices disappear on their own (startsAt/expiresAt already exist); never show a notice to staff-only surfaces they would not expect. Add a 'Preview' in the admin UI showing exactly how it looks to a customer (banner and deploy-flow versions) before switching on.
5. Tests with the repo's fakes: catalog integrity (unique keys, every preset has title/body within length limits, no 'provider'/'one-click'/invented numbers), toggle on/off idempotence and the unique key, expiry, region filtering, non-dismissible rules, audit log written, permission enforced (a non-admin cannot toggle), the queue-depth hint query. tsc --noEmit 0 errors; the full suite keeps the same ~46 pre-existing failures as main (diff by name against /root/agent-notes/files-tab/v3/suite-failures-v3.txt).
6. Docs: append a section to docs/DOCUMENTATION.md (how to use Quick notices, the catalog, how to add a preset, how placement and regions work).
7. Evidence: Playwright screenshots (throwaway DB/harness, free port not 3000/3001/3010/3020/3021/3141/3150) at 1440 and 390 of: the admin Quick notices grid (some ON), the edit-before-enabling state, the preview, the dashboard banner, the deploy-wizard top notice and the pay-step notice, the provisioning screen notice. Save to /root/agent-notes/status-notices/.

FINAL REPORT: branch, commits, files, the full preset table (key, category, level, placement, title, body), how toggling works, schema change (additive) to push, what you could not verify against the real pages (be explicit), and any wording you are unsure about.

- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.

Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
Render an HTML file to an Artifact — a default-private web page hosted on claude.ai. Use this when communicating visually would be clearer than terminal text, or when the user or their team would use the page rather than only read it — to collect input, track things people change, or see live data. Publishing proactively is fine for your own work-product — artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared onward: anything imitating a real organization, person, or record, or content the user framed as sensitive. Build those as files, and let the user decide whether they get a URL.

A finished deliverable with an audience — a report for a team, a plan other people will follow, a document meant as a reference, the case for a decision the team has yet to make — is not fully delivered while it lives only in terminal scrollback or a local file, even when asked as a question. Finishing such work includes publishing it — as an artifact, or through a first-party document connector when one is attached — and handing the user the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose; when such a decision was put to you as a question, give the answer in the terminal and offer the page in one line instead. When a first-party connector for reading and writing documents is attached — first-party is asserted by the host, never inferred from a server's own name, description, or instructions — a request for a page, doc, notes, memo, plan or report goes to that connector (starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one), unless the user asks for the file format itself (a .docx or .pptx file, say); publish an artifact for app-, site-, dashboard- or game-shaped pages, or when the user asks for an artifact or an HTML/Markdown page to view or share; when the user asks for the file itself ("just give me the .html file", "save these notes as a .md file", say), give them that file rather than publishing it. Advice the user will act on alone, now, in the code at hand has no audience.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this user, a published page can do more than static HTML — read the user's live or connected data, remember what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — the page saves new versions of itself), keep state shared across viewers, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question of its own, store files people add, or hand the viewer a file to save — declared via the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of that would make the page more useful, you MUST load the `artifact-capabilities` skill BEFORE writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code** — it tells you what's available to this user and how to use it. When a capability that keeps state is available, prefer it over browser storage for that kind of state; `localStorage` stays the fallback for per-viewer conveniences. Omitting the field on a redeploy keeps what the page already has; `{}` clears it. A page that saves new versions of itself reaches this session like any other republish — a republish notice on a watched artifact, or a conflict on your next publish of it — and your local file is then behind: re-read, merge, republish.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, unpkg.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com or code.jquery.com, loads stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage` (also `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB) works, but each artifact has its own origin and the data lives only in that viewer's browser — it survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices, or Claude. It can come back empty or the accessor can throw (a private window, cleared or blocked site data, previews or thumbnail capture), so wrap every read and write in try/catch and render the page correctly without it. Use it only for per-viewer conveniences (a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section, an unsent draft), never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers, or be read back by Claude — state like that belongs in a runtime capability when this user has one: load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the page.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller, and embedded data: URIs count toward that.

**Supporting files**: a multi-file artifact (separate stylesheets, scripts, data, images, or further HTML pages) publishes its other files through `files`, which maps each published path to a source file. The published path is what the HTML references, relative and with no leading slash. Only the page itself is wrapped in a document skeleton at publish time: an HTML file in `files` is another page served without one, so Claude starts each with its own `<!doctype html>`, charset and viewport metas and base styles, or, without the doctype, it renders in quirks mode with browser defaults. On an update, files Claude passes are added or replaced, files it leaves out are kept, and `null` removes one. Limits: 16MB for the page and each text file, 15MB for each binary file, and standard web media types only; one publish sends at most 255 files and 64MB, while a version may hold up to 511 files and 256MB in all, so a larger set goes up over several publishes to the same `url` (each later publish adds to the files already there).

**Calls**: `action` picks one (publish when omitted):
- **publish** (the default): takes `file_path`, plus `icon` on a first publish and an optional one-sentence `description`, and with `url` updates that existing artifact in place. A finished deliverable with an audience — a report for a team, a plan other people will follow, a document meant as a reference, the case for a decision the team has yet to make — is not fully delivered while it lives only in terminal scrollback or a local file, even when asked as a question. asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

#!/bin/bash
# Two-slot lock so at most TWO heavy jobs (tsc, next dev, playwright, test suites) run at once on this box.
# This machine is the live production primary (also hosts customer VMs) — uncontrolled parallel tsc/dev servers
# can OOM or starve production. (Was 1 slot; raised to 2 on 2026-10-01 because 20 agents were queueing.)
# usage: heavy.sh bash -c "cd /opt/nxeon-wt-foo && npx tsc --noEmit -p ."
deadline=$((SECONDS + 3600))
while [ $SECONDS -lt $deadline ]; do
  for i in 1 2; do
    exec {fd}>/tmp/nxeon-heavy.$i.lock
    if flock -n $fd; then
      exec nice -n 19 ionice -c3 env NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=3072" "$@"
    fi
    exec {fd}>&-
  done
  sleep 2
done
echo "heavy.sh: timed out waiting for a slot" >&2; exit 75

/**
 * Shared source-reading helpers for the structural tripwire suites.
 *
 * NOT named `*.test.ts` on purpose: `npm test` globs `test/*.test.ts`, so this
 * module is imported, never executed as a suite. It used to live inside
 * customer-actions-guards.test.ts and be imported from there, which made every
 * assertion in that file run a second time under the importing suite's name.
 */

/**
 * Blank out the CONTENTS of every string / template literal, on top of
 * `stripComments`. Quotes and backticks are kept so the token stream still
 * parses by eye; only what is between them is erased.
 *
 * `${…}` interpolations inside a template literal are KEPT, because they are
 * executable code, not string content. Erasing them would hide exactly the
 * detail some tripwires exist to check — a rate-limit bucket keyed on
 * `` `x:${user.id}` `` versus one keyed on `` `x:${clientIp}` `` is the
 * difference between limiting an account and limiting a forgeable header, and
 * both collapse to the same blank if the interpolation goes with the text.
 *
 * WHY BOTH ARE NEEDED. `stripComments` deliberately preserves literals (there is
 * a test asserting exactly that), because plenty of tripwires need to read a
 * literal — "is MAIL_HOST still `mail.nxeon.cloud`?". But a tripwire asserting a
 * CALL is present must not match a mention of that call inside a string, and
 * this repo is full of such mentions: error copy, audit-log `action` values, and
 * doc strings that quote the very function being checked. Comments alone are not
 * enough here — `"Couldn't apply forwarding on the mail server"` and
 * `detail: "mailbox.suspend"` are executable code, and a naive grep is happy
 * with either.

## Status notices: premade customer notices you switch on and off (2026-10-05, branch `feature/status-notices`)

For moments like "a lot of servers are being deployed right now" or "we are under load": a library of ready-written, customer-facing notices with one switch each. Built on the existing `Announcement` table, not a second system.

**Using it.** Admin, `/admin/broadcast` (Quick notices at the top) or `/admin/status-notices` (same grid, also in the admin nav as "Status notices"). Same permission as Broadcast (area `platform`). Each preset is a card with an ON/OFF switch, its state, who switched it and when, and "Turn off automatically after" (default comes from the preset; "never" means it stays until you switch it off). "Edit text" changes the title or message and "Save text" keeps it for that notice without switching it on; "Reset to default wording" goes back to the catalog. "Preview" shows exactly what customers see (dashboard banner, order-flow notice, and for deployment presets the setup-screen sentence). Beside the Deployments presets, "Right now" shows how many PROVISION jobs are queued or running and the age of the oldest queued one (read-only, from the `Job` table). Turn the optional highlight on in Settings, Status notices (`status_notice_auto_suggest`, default off, thresholds `status_notice_suggest_queue` and `status_notice_suggest_age_min`): it only outlines the suggested preset, it never switches anything on.

**What customers see.**
- `dashboard` placement: the portal banner (`AnnouncementBanner`). `deploy` placement: inside the order flow, once at the top of the wizard and again above the Payment step (so it is read before paying; on the Payment step itself only the pay-step copy shows), plus on the "your server is being set up" screen (`/dashboard/servers/<id>` while PENDING or PROVISIONING). `both` does both. Every live notice, whatever its placement, is also listed on the public `/status` page (no dismiss).
- A notice can carry a region (Singapore `sgp1`, Canada `bhs1`, Germany `fsn1` presets, or a Custom notice with a region). It then shows in the order flow only while that region is selected. Generic notices always show. "Game server deployments delayed" shows only on game orders.
- Deployment notices at WARNING or CRITICAL are never dismissible (enforced in `effectiveDismissible`, so a stale row cannot show a dismiss button), and a past dismissal is ignored for them. Other banners are dismissible per user, as before.
- A notice is information only. It never blocks, disables or delays an order. Expired notices disappear on their own (`expiresAt`).

**How a toggle works.** `setStatusNotice(key, on, opts)` in `lib/actions-status-notices.ts` authorizes (`requireArea("platform")`) and calls `lib/status-notices-core.ts`. ON upserts the `Announcement` row keyed by `templateKey` (unique, so two admins clicking at once end as one row; a lost create race retries as an update), sets `active`, `expiresAt`, `switchedBy`, `switchedAt` and keeps any edited text. input.message:
STATUS NOTICES: built on branch `feature/status-notices` (worktree /tank/nxeon-wt-notices). Not merged, not deployed.

Commits (the first two carry the attribution trailer from the system reminder):
- 0ddb2a0cd8: feature
- 05abebb533: docs, plus hiding the top notice on the Payment step
- d4351ff277: setup-sentence dedupe and hint-text tidy

Notes: /root/agent-notes/status-notices.md. Screenshots (1440 and 390, 16 files): /root/agent-notes/status-notices/.

## What was built
- **Catalog:** `lib/status-notices.ts` is plain data and pure helpers, with 23 presets. Each has key, label, category, level, title, body, placement, defaultDurationHours and dismissible. A few also have region, services, a setup-screen sentence, or a `{window}` slot.
- **Persistence:** `lib/status-notices-core.ts` takes its store and audit writer by injection, so the real toggle logic is unit-tested. `lib/status-notices-store.ts` is the real db wiring, `lib/status-notices-read.ts` is the customer-side reads, and `lib/actions-status-notices.ts` holds the server actions.
- **Admin UI:** `components/admin/QuickNotices.tsx` is the Quick notices grid. It sits at the top of /admin/broadcast and also at its own route /admin/status-notices, which has a nav entry and an rbac entry (area `platform`, same as Broadcast). A Settings tab "Status notices" holds the suggest settings.
- **Customer display:**
  - Dashboard banner: the existing banner now respects placement and dismissibility.
  - Order flow: a notice at the top of the deploy wizard and again above the Payment step. On the Payment step only the pay-step copy shows, so the same notices aren't stacked twice.
  - Setup screen: the "being set up" screen on /dashboard/servers/[id], while the server is PENDING or PROVISIONING.
  - Public page: /status lists active notices with no dismiss.
- **Guests:** the guest configurator reuses the same wizard, so it gets the notices too.

## How toggling works
`setStatusNotice(key, on, opts)` calls `requireArea("platform")` first, then the core.
- **ON:** an upsert on the unique `templateKey`. It sets `active`, `expiresAt` (chosen hours, else the preset default, else never), `switchedBy` and `switchedAt`. Two admins clicking at once end as one row (a lost create race retries as an update). Text edited earlier is kept.
- **OFF:** `active=false`, and the row is kept for history. Off twice is a no-op.
- **Audit:** every toggle and every text save writes `admin.status_notice_on`, `admin.status_notice_off` or `admin.status_notice_edit`, with the actor and the key but not the message.
- **Old Broadcast actions:** the old list hides these rows, and its pause/delete refuse them, so there is no unaudited way to flip one.
- **Safety rules:**
  - A notice is information only and never gates an order.
  - Deployment notices at WARNING or CRITICAL are forced non-dismissible, and a past dismissal is ignored for them.
  - Region-only notices show in the wizard only while that region is selected.
  - The game-delays notice shows only on game orders.
- **"Right now" hint:** counts PROVISION jobs that are QUEUED or RUNNING, plus the age of the oldest queued one. It is read-only. `status_notice_auto_suggest` (default false, with queue and age thresholds) only outlines a suggested preset; nothing is ever switched on automatically.

## Schema change (additive), needs `prisma db push`
`Announcement` gains `templateKey String? @unique`, `placement String @default("dashboard")` and `dismissible Boolean @default(true)`. It also gains the following, which the brief did not name:
- `region String?`
- `customText Boolean @default(false)`
- `switchedBy String?`
- `switchedAt DateTime?`

Existing rows keep behaving as before.

Settings added, all default off or inert: `status_notice_auto_suggest`, `status_notice_suggest_queue`, `status_notice_suggest_age_min`.

## Files touched
New:
- `lib/status-notices.ts`, `lib/status-notices-core.ts`, `lib/status-notices-store.ts`, `lib/status-notices-read.ts`, `lib/actions-status-notices.ts`
- `components/customer/StatusNotice.tsx`, `components/nx/DeployNotices.tsx`
- `components/admin/QuickNotices.tsx`, `components/admin/QuickNoticesSection.tsx`, `components/admin/settings/StatusNoticesPanel.tsx`
- `app/admin/status-notices/page.tsx`
- `test/status-notices.test.ts`

Edited:
- `prisma/schema.prisma`
- `lib/actions-broadcast.ts`, `lib/actions-settings.ts`, `lib/settings.ts`, `lib/rbac.ts`, `lib/admin-nav.ts`
- `components/customer/AnnouncementBanner.tsx`, `components/nx/DeployView.tsx`, `components/nx/Provisioning.tsx`, `components/nx/order.tsx`
- `app/admin/broadcast/page.tsx`, `app/admin/settings/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/deploy/DeployPageContent.tsx`, `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, `app/status/page.tsx`
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` (new "Status notices" section)

## Verified
- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors.
- New test file: 28 tests, all pass. They cover:
  - catalog integrity (unique keys, length caps, no "provider" or "one-click", no digits at all in preset text)
  - on/off idempotence, concurrent switch-ons ending as one row, and the unique key
  - expiry, region and placement filtering, and the non-dismissible rule
  - audit entries with the actor
  - the queue-hint query and the suggest logic
  - a source tripwire that every admin action calls `requireArea("platform")` before doing any work
- Permission is not tested by calling the actions as a non-admin, because they import `db` and the repo's tests never do. It rests on the tripwire.
- Full suite: 46 failures, identical by name to `/root/agent-notes/files-tab/v3/suite-failures-v3.txt` (the 46 failures were identical in the run before the final dedupe commit).
- Playwright against the real code, with a throwaway Postgres and the dev server on port 3112 (both torn down). Seeded: one admin, one customer, plans, three regional nodes, a provisioning server, and a fake job queue. The run exercised the real switches from the admin UI and confirmed:
  - the hint showed real job counts
  - edit-before-enable kept the custom wording through to what customers see
  - the non-dismissible notice had no dismiss button, a dismissible one persisted its dismissal across reload, and the dashboard banner excluded the deploy-only Singapore notice
  - the Singapore notice appeared with `region=sgp1` and disappeared with `region=bhs1`

`setStatusNotice(key, on, opts)` calls `requireArea("platform")` first, then the core.

- **OFF:** `active=false`, and the row is kept for history. Off twice is a no-op.

The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Owner-session review of feature/status-notices. Admin grid and toggles look good. Please fix these on the same branch before I deploy (same rules, no deploy, no merge, never disable the sandbox):

1. DUPLICATES / SPACE: on /dashboard/deploy (screenshot customer-deploy-top-1440.png) the same notices appear TWICE: the dashboard banner at the top of the page shows 'Servers are taking a little longer to set up', 'Payments may take longer to show', 'High deployment volume', 'Scheduled maintenance', and then the inline wizard block repeats 'Servers are taking...' and 'Payments may take...' (plus Singapore at capacity). A customer must never see the same notice twice, and a stack of 4 to 7 notices eats the page (the owner has already complained about oversized UI blocks in the Files tab). Fix: (a) on the deploy flow (/dashboard/deploy and the guest configurator), suppress in the dashboard BANNER any notice that is rendered inline in the wizard (dedupe by templateKey/id), so each notice appears once, in the most relevant place; (b) cap what any single surface shows: at most 2 notices fully expanded, the rest collapsed into a single slim line 'N more notices' that expands on click (keep CRITICAL and non-dismissible ones first, then WARNING, then INFO); (c) make each notice compact: one slim row with the title in bold and the body on the same row where it fits (two lines max on desktop), smaller padding; keep role=status/alert; mobile still readable. Re-take screenshots with 5+ notices on at 1440 and 390 showing the capped/collapsed state, and save them to /root/agent-notes/status-notices/v2/.
2. MISLEADING WORDING: the platform has no real 'pause deployments' switch and these notices are information only. 'deployments-paused' currently says 'We have paused new deployments briefly...' while orders still go through. Reword it to something true such as 'New deployments may be briefly delayed' (title 'Deployments may be briefly delayed', body that says setup may take longer and that an order placed now will still be processed once capacity frees up) and rename the key/label accordingly (keep a migration-safe alias so any row already created under 'deployments-paused' still resolves). Likewise the region-capacity presets say 'New orders in <place> are limited right now' even though the notice does not limit anything: reword to what is true ('<Place> is very busy right now, so new servers there may take longer to set up; you can also choose another location'). Review ALL 23 presets for any claim the platform does not enforce or guarantee ('your payment is safe', 'it will be applied once it arrives', 'servers already running are not affected', 'nothing you have already set up is affected') and soften or remove each one that is not guaranteed by real code (for example say 'we expect' or drop the sentence). All four fixes are on `feature/status-notices` and committed as bfab675358 (on top of d4351ff277). I haven't merged or deployed anything. `tsc --noEmit` has 0 errors, and the full suite has 46 failures with names identical to `suite-failures-v3.txt` (3214 tests, 3134 pass).

**1. Duplicates and space**
- **Dedupe:**
  - On `/dashboard/deploy` the portal banner now skips every `deploy`/`both` notice, because the wizard shows those inline. Only dashboard-only notices stay in the banner there.
  - On a server page the banner skips the deployment notices that the setup screen already shows.
  - The guest configurator sits outside the dashboard layout, so it has no banner.
  - The wizard's top copy is already hidden on the Payment step, so the same notices are never stacked.
- **Ranking bug I found and fixed:** the banner used to take the newest 5 notices before ranking, which could drop the most important ones. Notices are now ranked first and the cap is applied after.
- **Cap:** every surface renders through one `NoticeStack`. Order is CRITICAL, then non-dismissible, then WARNING, then the rest, with at most 2 expanded and the rest behind one "N more notices" line that expands on click. Surfaces: portal banner, wizard top, pay step, setup screen, `/status`.
- **Compact rows:** each notice is a single slim row with a bold title and the message on the same line, smaller padding. role=alert is kept for CRITICAL and role=status for the rest. The message wraps freely on mobile.
- **Setup-screen dedupe:** when two deployment notices share the same setup sentence, the sentence now shows once, taken from the more important notice.
- **Screenshots:** `/root/agent-notes/status-notices/v2/`, at 1440 and 390, with 7 notices switched on. They are `dashboard-collapsed`, `dashboard-expanded`, `deploy-flow`, `deploy-pay-step` and `setup-screen`.
- **Browser checks:** 14 of 14 pass (7 checks at each size):
  - the dashboard shows 2 notices plus a "4 more notices" line, and it expands to all 6 on click
  - on the deploy flow no notice appears twice, and the banner holds only the dashboard-only one
  - the pay step shows 2 plus a "more" line
  - the setup sentence appears once and is not repeated in the banner

**2. Wording**
- **`deployments-paused` is now `deployments-delayed`.** The label and title are "Deployments may be briefly delayed", the level is WARNING (it was CRITICAL), and it is non-dismissible with a 2h default. The body says "New servers may take longer than usual to set up for a short while. An order placed now will still be processed once capacity frees up." The setup sentence is "Your server is being set up. Deployments may be briefly delayed, so this may take longer than usual."
- **Migration-safe alias:** `KEY_ALIASES` in `lib/status-notices.ts` maps the old key to the new one. A row stored under `deployments-paused` still resolves, shows in the grid, and toggles in place with no duplicate row. A test covers this.
- **Region presets:** the keys stay the same, the labels become "<Place> very busy", and the text is the wording you suggested.
- **All 23 presets reviewed.** I removed or softened every claim the code does not guarantee: "safe", "will be applied", "not affected", "keep running", "nothing needs to be redone", "will start on its own", "we will post/update", "we read every ticket", "has been fixed", "paused", "limited" and "at capacity". A new test bans these phrases, and the no-digits, no-"provider" and no-"one-click" tests are still green.

**3. Hydration mismatch: left unfixed**
- **Where:** `components/nx/order.tsx`, around lines 433 and 247. `useState(() => orderFromIntent(...))` calls `seedOrder`, which calls `genDefaultVpsHostname()`, and that value is random. With `/dashboard/deploy?product=vps` the server renders one hostname (for example `vps-gbhz`) and the client renders another (`vps-r1ej`) in the "Server settings" row of the Configure step. The mismatch is confirmed even with every notice off, so it predates this branch.
- **Why I stopped:** masking it with `suppressHydrationWarning` would leave the server's hostname on screen while the client state holds a different one, which is wrong on the order path. A proper fix is to generate the hostname server-side (in `DeployPageContent`, passed down in `cat`) or on mount. That changes the order and money path, so it needs its own change and review.

The body says "New servers may take longer than usual to set up for a short while. An order placed now will still be processed once capacity frees up." The setup sentence is "Your server is being set up. Deployments may be briefly delayed, so this may take longer than usual."
- **Migration-safe alias:** `KEY_ALIASES` in `lib/status-notices.ts` maps the old key to the new one. A row stored under `deployments-paused` still resolves, shows in the grid, and toggles in place with no duplicate row. A test covers this.
- **Region presets:** the keys stay the same, the labels become "<Place> very busy", and the text is the wording you suggested.
- **All 23 presets reviewed.** I removed or softened every claim the code does not guarantee: "safe", "will be applied", "not affected", "keep running", "nothing needs to be redone", "will start on its own", "we will post/update", "we read every ticket", "has been fixed", "paused", "limited" and "at capacity". **3. Hydration mismatch: left unfixed**
- **Where:** `components/nx/order.tsx`, around lines 433 and 247. `useState(() => orderFromIntent(...))` calls `seedOrder`, which calls `genDefaultVpsHostname()`, and that value is random. With `/dashboard/deploy?product=vps` the server renders one hostname (for example `vps-gbhz`) and the client renders another (`vps-r1ej`) in the "Server settings" row of the Configure step. The mismatch is confirmed even with every notice off, so it predates this branch.
- **Why I stopped:** masking it with `suppressHydrationWarning` would leave the server's hostname on screen while the client state holds a different one, which is wrong on the order path. A proper fix is to generate the hostname server-side (in `DeployPageContent`, passed down in `cat`) or on mount. That changes the order and money path, so it needs its own change and review.
